clue.text: Tricks used to secure article by English national

indicators.note: the tricks are used to hold the article fast inside them, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: japes are pranks or tricks
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of using tricks to get hold of an item from an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to secure' signals a container; 'national' is the definition, a noun for a citizen, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Japan is a national of that country, so the word works as a noun for such a person.

clue.text: One line I found in Roman poet — short early work

indicators.note: the three small pieces are discovered sitting inside the poet's name
short tells us the poet's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Juvenal was the Roman satirical poet
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A scholar finds a single line in a Roman poet's writings, part of a brief youthful piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims JUVENAL to JUVENA, and 'found in' places I, L, I between its N and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Juvenilia are the works an author produced in youth, so the plural noun means early work collectively.

clue.text: Writes about Greek goddess and Roman gods

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: to pen is to write, so writes gives pens
Ate was the Greek goddess of folly and ruin

explanation.surface: Someone writes about a Greek goddess and also about the gods of Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals a container. Ate is a minor goddess of mischief, less familiar than the Olympians.
explanation.definitionFit: The Penates were the guardian deities of the Roman household and storeroom.

clue.text: Sound experienced, on old ship in US port

indicators.note: Sound at the start tells us a word is spoken and we write what we hear

parts.note: if you knew something you had experienced it
Noah's ark is the ancient vessel of the Bible

explanation.surface: A seasoned sailor aboard a historic vessel arrives in an American harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' applies only to 'experienced'. Newark, New Jersey, is a major American seaport.
explanation.definitionFit: Newark, New Jersey, has one of the busiest container seaports in the United States.

clue.text: Without starting to stare, amble round, sounding unofficial

indicators.note: the stroll is wrapped round the other piece

parts.note: an amble is a leisurely stroll

indicators.note: the stare word loses its opening letter, as it is going without its start

parts.note: to gawp is to stare open-mouthed

explanation.surface: Someone avoids gawping and goes for a walk while carrying out an informal survey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without starting' leaves AWP; 'round' then wraps the walking word around it. 'sounding' looks like a homophone signal but is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw poll is an informal, unofficial sounding of opinion taken by a quick show of views.

clue.text: Work steadily to restrict decline that's all too common?

indicators.note: the work word restricts, or hems in, the decline word

parts.note: to ply is to work steadily at a trade
to ebb is to decline or fade

explanation.surface: Working hard keeps a person from slipping into vulgar ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to restrict' signals a container. Plebby is British slang, from plebeian, for common or vulgar.
explanation.definitionFit: Plebby is British slang for vulgar or lower class, which the question mark presents as all too common.

clue.text: One out to describe, vividly, woman's lost cat

indicators.note: out tells us the one letter is removed from the describing word

parts.note: to paint something in words is to describe it vividly
the Roman numeral for one is I
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to give a vivid account of a woman's missing pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes the one, leaving PANT; 'lost' only adds to the picture of the missing pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A panther is a large wild feline, typically a leopard or a black jaguar.

clue.text: Anticipating pedant will dispute this?

parts.note: pedants object to anticipate being used to mean merely expect, so the word for waiting in hope is one they would quarrel with

explanation.surface: A fussy grammarian is expected to object to something.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on the pedantic objection that anticipate should mean forestall, not simply look forward to.
explanation.definitionFit: Expectant means waiting for something, which is the loose sense of anticipating that sticklers dispute.

clue.text: Solvent, and well regarded in Rome, adopting religion

indicators.note: adopting means taking the religion into the Italian word

parts.note: bene is Italian for well, as an Italian would put it
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A Roman with a good name, who is solvent, takes up a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopting' signals a container. Solvent misleads as financially sound; Italian bene means well.
explanation.definitionFit: Benzene is a colourless liquid hydrocarbon widely used as an industrial solvent.

clue.text: One leaving empty vehicle

indicators.note: leaving tells us the one letter goes away from the word for empty

parts.note: vain can mean empty or worthless, as in vain words
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A single person walks away from an unoccupied vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes I (One) out of VAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A van is a covered motor vehicle for carrying goods.

clue.text: It may have caused heated reaction in old pit

definitions.text: It may have caused heated reaction in old pit

parts.words: It may have caused heated reaction in old pit
parts.note: pit is slang for bed, and a lidded pan of hot coals was once run between the sheets to warm them, so its heat drew a reaction from the sleeper

explanation.surface: Something seems to have provoked an angry response in a disused mine.
explanation.walkthrough: Pit suggests a coal mine and heated reaction a row; in fact the pit is a bed and the heat is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A warming pan was a long-handled covered pan of embers used to heat a bed before sleeping.

clue.text: Won't burn turn a darkish colour?

indicators.note: turn tells us to turn the letters around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A cook hopes something that won't burn will still turn a deep shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges WONTBURN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nut-brown is the warm mid-to-dark brown of a ripe hazelnut.

clue.text: Wine you once rejected, being served game

parts.note: hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

indicators.note: rejected tells us the old word for you is turned back

parts.note: ye is the archaic form of you

explanation.surface: A guest turns down wine while being served game at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the old word backwards, giving EY. Game misleads as meat on the table; hock is British for Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hockey is a team sport, and game here means a sport played competitively.

clue.text: About to bunk off history period, possibly? Not so!

indicators.note: to bunk off is to skip away, so the about word goes missing

parts.note: a history period at school is an example of a lesson
on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A pupil is about to skip a history class, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bunk off' (British slang for skipping school) removes ON from LESSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Less means not so much, to a smaller degree, so it stands for not so.

clue.text: First of silly puns, perhaps wounding ripostes?

indicators.note: first of means take the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: puns are an example of wordplay

explanation.surface: Silly puns can serve as cutting comebacks.
explanation.walkthrough: A riposte is both a witty retort and a fencer's counter-thrust, so wounding ripostes are sword strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: In fencing a riposte is a counter-attack, and an exchange of such thrusts is fighting with blades.

clue.text: Needing jab, fellow went quickly about it, appearing calm

parts.note: a poke is a jab

indicators.note: about it means the speed word wraps round the fellow

parts.note: raced means went quickly

explanation.surface: Someone due an injection rushed past it while looking unruffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about it' signals a container. Jab misleads as an injection; it is just a prod.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker-faced means showing no emotion, the impassive look of a card player hiding a hand.

clue.text: Turned right, having studied map

parts.note: on a standard map the right-hand side is one compass point, so turning right after reading it sends you in that direction

explanation.surface: A traveller checks the map and then turns right.
explanation.walkthrough: Maps are drawn with north at the top, so right is the direction of sunrise.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading east is what a traveller does on turning to the right-hand side of a conventional map.

clue.text: Superlative effort by women to keep study up on time

indicators.note: the women keep the study within them

parts.note: dames are women

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the study word reads upwards

parts.note: a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Women make a supreme effort to keep up their studies on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the study word over, giving NED, and 'to keep' signals a container. One does one's damnedest.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing your damnedest means making your utmost effort, and the word is itself a superlative form.

clue.text: Eventually producing larger shoes?

definitions.meaning: in the end, after a long wait
a last is a shoemaker's foot-shaped form, and a long one would make big shoes

explanation.surface: In the end a cobbler starts making bigger footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means finally after much delay, and read literally it describes using an extended shoe form.

clue.text: Up to this point, being beaten hurts, footballers admitted

indicators.note: the scrambled letters admit, or let in, the footballers
being beaten means the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: FA is the Football Association, governing body of English football

explanation.surface: So far the injured footballers have conceded that losing hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being beaten' rearranges to THUSR, and 'admitted' signals a container. The FA is English football's governing body.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus far is an idiom meaning until now or as far as this stage.

clue.text: Irish lad seen to continue running about round ship

indicators.note: about means the continue phrase goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to go on is to continue running
SS is the abbreviation for steamship
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An Irish boy is seen jogging on around a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals a container. Gossoon is Irish English for a boy, from French garçon.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossoon is an Irish English word for a boy or young lad, from French garçon.

clue.text: Call time

definitions.meaning: to call is to name or designate
a period of time, such as a school or prison sentence

explanation.definitionFit: Term as a verb means to name, and as a noun a fixed period such as a school session.

clue.text: Only half like an Arab that's clever, and not easily rattled

indicators.note: only half means keep just the first half of the word

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse, so like one is equine
able means clever or capable

explanation.surface: A clever Arab is only partly even-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: An Arab here is the horse breed; 'Only half' keeps EQU. The surface wants a person from Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: Equable means calm and even-tempered, someone hard to unsettle.

clue.text: Here's where it's to be found, in confidence

definitions.text: Here's where it's to be found
definitions.meaning: it is slang for gin or drink, which is kept in a glass vessel

explanation.surface: This is where to find it, told as a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle is the container for gin, and also British slang for courage or nerve.

clue.text: Is leading host's visitor almost keeping impulses in check?

indicators.note: keeping means the visitor word holds the impulses inside
almost means the visitor word loses its final letter

parts.note: a host's visitor is a guest
in Freudian psychology the id is the seat of instinctive impulses

explanation.surface: A guest restrains himself while the host shows the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' leaves GUES and 'keeping' signals a container; the id is Freud's seat of instinctive impulses.
explanation.definitionFit: Guides is the third-person verb meaning leads, so it stands for is leading.

clue.text: Unqualified to be considered by comprehensive?

explanation.surface: A pupil leaving a comprehensive school without qualifications is judged.
explanation.walkthrough: Comprehensive and unqualified suggest a British state secondary school and exam results, but both are adjectives meaning total.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute means total and unconditional, a sense shared by unqualified and comprehensive.

clue.text: Play another club, perhaps, in due course

definitions.text: Play another club, perhaps, in due course

parts.words: Play another club, perhaps, in due course
parts.note: at cards, laying a club after a club has been led is matching the led suit, which you do in turn

explanation.surface: A team will take on a different side when the time comes.
explanation.walkthrough: Club and play suggest a sports fixture, but this is a card game where you must match the suit led.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to play a card of the suit led, and figuratively to do as others have done.

clue.text: Stay out of round, having one extra

definitions.meaning: in a knockout competition a competitor without an opponent sits a round out and goes through
in cricket a run scored without the ball touching the bat or batsman is one of the extras

explanation.surface: Someone sits out a round of drinks after having one too many.
explanation.definitionFit: A bye is a free pass to the next round, and in cricket a run conceded past the wicketkeeper.

clue.text: Producer of sketch needs primarily comic material

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of the next word

parts.note: rayon is a synthetic fabric

explanation.surface: A comedy sketch writer needs mainly funny material.
explanation.walkthrough: Sketch and comic suggest a comedy routine, but the sketch is a drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayon is a stick of coloured wax used to make drawings, so it produces a sketch.

clue.text: She's in a minor depression, as supporter of party

indicators.note: in means the woman's word goes inside the depression

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow in a surface
her stands for she

explanation.surface: A woman feeling slightly down is a loyal member of a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals a container. Depression misleads as low mood; it is a small hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower or supporter of a cause, faction or party.
